_meta.coder: SEC AI-incident disclosure coding, Tesla batch b07
_meta.baseline_evidence: T3 same-family baseline is established for every fiscal year spanning these incidents. Tesla's 10-Ks each carry Autopilot/FSD automated-driving risk-factor language, and every incident's 12-month window contains at least one such 10-K plus quarterly 10-Qs. FY2019 10-K (ACCESSION 0001564590-20-004475, filed 2020-02-13, Item 1A): 'Our vehicles have been involved and we expect in the future will be involved in crashes resulting in death or personal injury, and such crashes where Autopilot or FSD features are engaged are the subject of significant public attention'; also 'claims arising from or related to misuse or claimed failures of new technologies ... including Autopilot and FSD' and self-driving regulatory-uncertainty language. FY2021 10-K (0000950170-22-000796, filed 2022-02-07) and FY2022 10-K (0000950170-23-001409, filed 2023-01-31) carry equivalent language, the FY2022 filing adding 'regulatory scrutiny arising from or related to misuse or claimed failures or alleged misrepresentations of such new technologies' and reference to 'NHTSA's Standing General Order requiring reports regarding crashes involving vehicles with advanced driver assistance systems.'
_meta.negative_search_evidence: EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov, ciks=0001318605) returned NO in-window filing naming any single incident here or its specific legal/regulatory consequence: 'rolling stop'=0 hits; 'phantom braking'=0 hits; 'first responder'=1 hit (a 2026 8-K, out of window); 'false advertising' and 'Department of Motor Vehicles'=hits only from 2010-2012 (early dealership/franchise matters, not the 2021 CA-DMV Autopilot action). Tesla does not itemize individual crashes or product-liability suits in its filings. A U.S. DOJ investigation into Autopilot/FSD IS disclosed ('requests from the DOJ') in the FY2022 10-K and 2023 10-Qs, but it is a general Autopilot/FSD probe, not tied to any specific incident in this batch.
